rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كيف asks about a state or manner, equivalent to asking in what condition someone is.
rows.anchor: كيف بمعنى: على أي حال، تقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here كيف conveys astonishment at people denying God after being dead and then brought to life.
rows.anchor: وتقع بمعنى: التعجب، في مثل قوله:

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says لات resembles ليس in some settings but is less flexible: it lacks the latter's use with explicit persons and absent predicates.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: (لات) مشبهة (بليس) في بعض المواضع،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some allow حين in the nominative by treating لات like ليس, though rarely; Ibn Qutayba says the accusative is stronger, and poets also attest genitive.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم يقول: ولات حين مناص. فيرفع، لأنها عنده

rows.speaker: أبو زبيد الطائي
rows.claim: Abu Zubayd's verse has لات governing the genitive time noun أوان.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زبيد الطائي : طلبوا صلحنا ولات أوان ... فأجبنا

rows.speaker: شاعر آخر
rows.claim: Another poet uses لات before ساعة in the genitive, attesting that the particle governs a time expression.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : فلما علمت أنني قد قتلته ... ندمت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لات operates with expressions of time; outside temporal expressions it has no grammatical effect.
rows.anchor: وإنما تكون (لات) مع الأحيان وتعمل فيها.

rows.speaker: بعض البغداديين
rows.claim: Some Baghdadi grammarians say tāʾ is added to حين أوان or الآن, with لا separate; they cite تحين without لا and verses with تحين and تلانا.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض البغداديين: (التاء) تزاد في أول (حين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba rejects the Baghdadi account because Arabs put the following noun in the genitive with لات, treating it as governed by the particle.
rows.anchor: وجر العرب بها يفسد عليه هذا المذهب، لأنهم إذا جروا

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī explains تحين as العاطفونه حين, with hāʾ becoming tāʾ in connected speech; he gives a parallel for تلانا.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي في قوله الشاعر: العاطفون تحين ما من عاطف

rows.speaker: الكلابي
rows.claim: A Kalābī speaker says حسبك تلان, intending حسبك الآن; connection turns final hāʾ into tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال: وسمعت الكلابي ينهى رجلا عن عمل، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says he will discuss pausing on لات and similar added tāʾs in his book on readings.
rows.anchor: وسنبين: كيف الوقوف عليها وعلى أمثالها من التاءات الزوائد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتاب originally denotes what God wrote on the Preserved Tablet concerning what will come to pass.
rows.anchor: ما كتبه الله في اللوح مما هو كائن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتب can mean decreed or settled, as when God decreed victory, allotted fate, or those destined for death.
rows.anchor: ثم تتفرع منه معان ترجع إلى هذا الأصل. كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse and other commands, كتب means prescribed as an obligation.
rows.anchor: ويكون كتب بمعنى فرض، كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتب may mean made or placed, as when God placed faith in people's hearts.
rows.anchor: ويكون كتب بمعنى جعل، كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the command to enter the Holy Land, كتب لكم means God commanded them to enter it.
rows.anchor: أي: أمركم أن تدخلوها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also gives the sense that God made the Holy Land for Abraham's descendants.
rows.anchor: ويقال: كتب هاهنا أيضا: جعل. يريد ادخلوا الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abraham saw people sinning in the realm of dominion and prayed against them; God told him to stop, since a servant might have good offspring, repent, or face the Fire.
rows.anchor: فروي: أنه رأى في الملكوت عبدا على فاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba rejects reading Abraham's words as sincere belief that a star was God: after seeing the kingdom to gain certainty he could not then believe the star was his Lord.
rows.anchor: أفترى الله أراه الملكوت ليوقن، فلما أيقن رأى كوكبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By استعارة, رحمة in the wind-and-rain verse means rain; خزائن رحمة and opened mercy mean stores of provision and provision granted.
rows.anchor: وقد توضع (الرحمة) موضع (المطر) لأنه ينزل برحمته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tongue can stand for speech; Abraham's لسان صدق means good remembrance, while a poet uses لسان for unwelcome news.
rows.anchor: ومن الاستعارة: اللسان يوضع موضع القول، لأن القول يكون بها.

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses لسان to mean a report or news that brings no pleasure.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر : إني أتتني لسان لا أسر بها ...

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذكر can stand for honor because the honored person is remembered; the Quran is a distinction for the Prophet and his people, and ذكركم means your honor.
rows.anchor: ومنه الذكر يوضع موضع الشرف، لأن الشريف يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ذكر means the people's honor or distinction, not simply a reminder.
rows.anchor: بل أتيناهم بذكرهم فهم عن ذكرهم معرضون [المؤمنون: 71]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forbidding even أف means not to find any part of one's parents' affairs burdensome, grow resentful, or speak harshly.
rows.anchor: أي لا تستثقل شيئا من أمرهما، وتضق به صدرا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أف began as an exhalation to blow away dust or ash, or clear a place to sit; it became an expression for anything burdensome.
rows.anchor: وأصل هذا نفخك للشيء يسقط عليك من تراب أو رماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أف would be stopped with sukūn, but takes a vowel to avoid meeting two quiescent sounds; it may be nunnated or not and may take other vowels.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن يسكن هذا، إلا أنه يحرك لاجتماع الساكنين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindling a fire for war means stirring up harm and planning to fight the Prophet; God extinguishing it means He subdued and weakened their effort.
rows.anchor: يريد كلما هاجوا شرا وأجمعوا أمرا ليحاربوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a following answer, لولا can mean هلا, as in the rebuke about earlier peoples and the poet's question why they do not count the armed hero.
rows.anchor: لولا تكون في بعض الأحوال بمعنى: هلا وذلك إذا رأيتها بغير جواب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an answer, لولا marks a condition whose result would occur but for another circumstance: Jonah would have remained until resurrection but for glorifying God.
rows.anchor: فإذا رأيت للولا جوابا فليست بهذا المعنى، كقوله:

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take لولا in the believing-town verse to mean لم: no town believed in time to benefit from faith except Jonah's people.
rows.anchor: وبعض المفسرين يجعل لولا في قوله: فلولا كانت قرية آمنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وحي broadly means any conveyed indication: speech, writing, gesture, or a message; sending revelation to prophets is one instance, with Gabriel bringing the Quran.
rows.anchor: كل شيء دللت به من كلام أو كتاب أو إشارة أو رسالة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Zachariah's story, فأوحى إليهم means he gestured to them; Ibn Qutayba prefers this over the reported gloss wrote to them.
rows.anchor: فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا [مريم: 11] ، أي أشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers gesture because another verse describes the sign as not speaking except by رمز, movements of the lips, brows, or eyes, which is not writing.
rows.anchor: والرمز: تحريك الشفتين أو الحاجبين أو العينين، ولا يكون كتابا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وحي can mean inspiration: God inspired the disciples and the bees.
rows.anchor: والوحي: إلهام، كقوله: وإذ أوحيت إلى الحواريين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وحي also denotes communication through a dream.
rows.anchor: والوحي: إعلام في المنام، كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb can mean Satanic whispering or prompting, including devils prompting one another with deceptive speech.
rows.anchor: والوحي: إعلام بالوسوسة من الشيطان، قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وحي can mean command: God commanded the earth to settle; a rajaz poet's phrase likewise means order it to stay still.
rows.anchor: والوحي: أمر، قال الله تعالى: بأن ربك أوحى لها (5)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition لام can stand where إلى is expected: أوحى لها means أوحى إليها, as confirmed by the verse about God inspiring the bees.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى: بأن ربك أوحى لها (5) [الزلزلة: 5] ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise هدانا لهذا means هدانا إلى هذا; other verses use إلى explicitly with هداه.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى: الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا [الأعراف: 43] ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes a truthful legacy among later people while arguing that scholarly investigation is needed to uncover hidden meanings in proverbs, idioms, and transmitted reports.
rows.anchor: لولا العلماء المنقبون في البلاد، المنقرون عن الخبء، الناظرون للخلوف،

rows.speaker: شاعر مجهول
rows.claim: An unattributed poem depicts an echo in a desolate scene, distant in the dark of night, as an example of deceptive perception.
rows.anchor: وصرماء مذكار كأن دويها ... بعيد جنان الليل مما يخيل

rows.speaker: شاعر مجهول
rows.claim: A second unattributed verse says humanlike speech, once heard, proves too indistinct to understand clearly.
rows.anchor: حديث أناسي فلما سمعته ... إذا ليس فيه ما أبين فأعقل

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal says a yearling fox in the desert looks like an armored horse when it climbs a rise, illustrating small things appearing large.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخطل يذكر فلاة رأى الصغير فيها كبيرا : ترى الثعلب الحولي فيها

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha says a herder carrying a load seems like a bird from his high, protected site, because height alters appearance.
rows.anchor: وقال النابغة : وحلت بيوتي في يفاع ممنع ... تخال به راعي

rows.speaker: ابن أحمر
rows.claim: Ibn Ahmar describes imagined shapes multiplying and a chameleon seeming to feed by pecking, as evidence of perceptual exaggeration.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أحمر أيضا في تضاعف الأعداد: وازدادت الأشباح أخيلة ...

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He likens professed belief paired with evasion to someone who pretends to take only morning drink while secretly gulping it down.
rows.anchor: وأخشى أن يكون معتقدا هذا والقائل به، يرفق عن صبوح ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in resurrection and the Prophet's report entails accepting barzakh torment; belief in divine questioning entails the angels' questioning in the grave.
rows.anchor: وما على من آمن بالبعث من الممات: أن يؤمن بعذاب البرزخ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who accepts Satan and jinn exist should also accept possession and their uncanny sounds or forms, as consistent implications of their existence.
rows.anchor: وما على من آمن بإنية الشيطان: أن يؤمن بتخبطه؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects calling Arabs universally ignorant or liars: scripture, prophets, earlier revelations, and peoples elsewhere corroborate what is reported.
rows.anchor: وما أخرجه إلى تجهيل العرب قاطبة وتكذيبها: وشاهدها على صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran treats jinn as one of two accountable peoples, addresses them, calls them men, and indicates relations with humans.
rows.anchor: قد جعل الله الجن أحد الثقلين، وخاطبهم في الكتاب كما خاطبنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of jinn heard the Quran and returned to warn their people; the Quran also describes Satan's touch as causing madness, hence مس.
rows.anchor: وأخبرنا عن طائفة منهم سمعوا القرآن فولوا إلى قومهم منذرين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites sound reports from the Prophet and early Muslims about the unseen attendant and related beings.
rows.anchor: هذا مع أخبار كثيرة صحاح تؤثر عن الرسول، صلى الله عليه وسلم، وعن السلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows that unusual events may occur in deserts, but says these incidents do not disprove realities people hear and see.
rows.anchor: وما ننكر مع هذا الفلوات قد يعرض فيها ما يذكرون، ولكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تطلع على الأفئدة means that the Fire rises over or looms above the hearts, like someone who climbs a mountain and overlooks it.
rows.anchor: قوله: تطلع على الأفئدة أي توفي عليها وتشرف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts are singled out because pain reaching the heart kills; the damned endure a deathlike condition without actually dying, as in the verse about Hell.
rows.anchor: وخص الأفئدة، لأن الألم إذا صار إلى الفؤاد مات صاحبه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نسيان may mean loss of memory, its basic opposite of retaining or remembering, as in the forgotten fish and Moses' request not to be blamed for forgetting.
rows.anchor: ضد الحفظ، كقوله: فإني نسيت الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نسيان can also mean abandonment: Adam abandoned the command; people abandoned belief in Judgment, God abandoned them, and believers should not forsake kindness.
rows.anchor: والنسيان: الترك، كقول الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رجز means torment; Pharaoh's people use it for the affliction God lifts, and Satan's rجز is so called because his guile causes punishment.
rows.anchor: الرجز: العذاب. قال الله تعالى- حكاية عن قوم فرعون:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رجس literally means stench or filth; unbelief and hypocrisy are called رجسا because they are foul.
rows.anchor: والرجس: النتن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the command to shun idols, الرجز denotes idols, named for the torment they bring about.
rows.anchor: والرجز فاهجر (5) [المدثر: 5] ، يعني الأوثان، سماها رجزا-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable is of the believer's heart and the light of faith and Quran placed in it; God's being the light of heaven and earth means people there find guidance by His light.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله لقلب المؤمن، وما أودعه بالإيمان والقرآن

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes take مثل نوره as the light in the believer's heart.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: مثل نوره، يعني في قلب المؤمن. كذلك قال المفسرون.

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba's father recited مثل نور المؤمن instead of مثل نوره; the report is transmitted through Ubayd Allah ibn Musa and Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas and Abu al-Aliya.
rows.anchor: وكان أبي يقرأ: الله نور السموات والأرض مثل نور المؤمن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مشكاة is a non-through niche; its مصباح is a lamp inside a glass vessel.
rows.anchor: كمشكاة، وهي: الكوة غير النافذة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glass seems like a bright, sparkling star because of its whiteness and sheen.
rows.anchor: القنديل كأنه من شدة بياضه وتلألئه، كوكب دري،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The olive tree is neither in sun all day nor shade all day; it receives both at different times, making it flourish, bear more, and yield purer oil.
rows.anchor: أي لا بارزة للشمس كل النهار ولا غربية لا مستترة في الظل كل النهار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran came down in stages across twenty-three years to ease people into duties, awaken them with recurring admonition, and test submission and discernment through abrogation.
rows.anchor: وأما تكرار الأنباء والقصص، فإن الله تبارك وتعالى أنزل القرآن نجوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though تثبيت addresses the Prophet, it is intended for him and the believers; repeated revelation also prevents people tiring of one long admonition.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للنبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم، والمراد بالتثبيت هو والمؤمنون.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet attended to his companions with admonition at intervals so they would not weary, especially when heedlessness and hardened hearts set in.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، يتخول أصحابه بالموعظة مخافة السآمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single simultaneous revelation would precede its occasions, burden Muslims and converts with all duties at once, erase reminders, and make staged abrogation impossible.
rows.anchor: ولو أتاهم القرآن نجما واحدا لسبق حدوث الأسباب التي أنزله الله بها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People need not memorize the whole Quran or complete a full reading; they should act on clear passages, believe ambiguous ones, obey commands, avoid prohibitions, and recite what they can in prayer.
rows.anchor: ولم يفرض الله على عباده أن يحفظوا القرآن كله، ولا أن يختموه في التعلم،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Quran was sent down to be acted upon, but people made reciting it their act.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: نزل القرآن ليعمل به، فاتخذ الناس تلاوته عملا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Companions learned portions rather than the whole Quran; only a few were enabled to collect and memorize it all.
rows.anchor: وكان أصحاب رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، ورضي عنهم- وهم مصابيح الأرض

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that a man who had recited al-Baqara and Al Imran was held in great esteem by the Companions.
rows.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: كان الرجل إذا قرأ البقرة وآل عمران جد فينا.

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali died without having collected the Quran.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي: توفى أبو بكر، وعمر، وعلي، رحمهم الله، ولم يجمعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal contexts خاف may mean knew, since fear contains an element of knowledge; this applies to a potentially unjust bequest and failure to keep God's limits.
rows.anchor: وقوله: فمن خاف من موص جنفا أو إثما [البقرة: 182] ، أي علم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رجا can mean fear: not hoping God has majesty means not fearing it, since hope is uncertain and retains an element of fear.
rows.anchor: و (رجوت) بمعنى: (خفت) . قال الله سبحانه:

rows.speaker: الهذلي
rows.claim: A Hudhali poet uses لم يرج of a bee sting to mean he did not fear it.
rows.anchor: قال الهذلي : إذا لسعته النحل لم يرج لسعها ...

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يئس can mean knew, because certainty of one thing makes a person despair of its alternative.
rows.anchor: و (يئست) بمعنى: (علمت) من قول الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid uses يئس for knowing what became apparent, after which the archers abandon other possibilities.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد : حتى إذا يئس الرماة فأرسلوا ...

rows.speaker: شاعر آخر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses ألم تيئسوا to mean did you not know I am Ibn Faris Zahdam.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : أقول لهم بالشعب إذ يأسرونني ...

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this inverted construction, مخلف وعده رسله means failing His messengers by breaking His promise to them.
rows.anchor: كقول الله تعالى: فلا تحسبن الله مخلف وعده رسله [إبراهيم: 47] ،

words: فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّۭ لِّىٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inverted phrasing فإنهم عدو لي means فإني عدو لهم, since anyone a person opposes opposes him in return.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله سبحانه: فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين (77) [الشعراء: 77]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order then drew near and descended is inverted: he descended to approach and drew near by descending.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله: ثم دنا فتدلى (8) [النجم: 8] أي: تدلى فدنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person has testimony from his own self: his limbs witness against him, and the person stands for those limbs.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله سبحانه: بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة (14) [القيامة: 14]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet reverses the relation: the ox's head is hidden by the shade while the rest stays in sun, so he says the shade entered over its head.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : ترى الثور فيها مدخل الظل رأسه ...

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom عرض الناقة على الحوض reverses the relation and intends عرض الحوض على الناقة, since each is presented to the other.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول: (اعرض الناقة على الحوض) تريد:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إمام originally means something or someone one follows; Abraham is imam because people follow and emulate his practice.
rows.anchor: أصله ما ائتممت به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A book can be called imam because people follow its record; in the verse about being summoned by their imam, it means the book containing their deeds.
rows.anchor: ثم يجعل الكتاب إماما يؤتم بما أحصاه. قال الله عز وجل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين, imam means a book or the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وقال: وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين [يس: 12] يعني:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A road can be called imam because travelers follow it and use it for guidance; the two towns lay beside a clear road.
rows.anchor: وقد يجعل الطريق إماما، لأن المسافر يأتم به ويستدل.
